messages:
incbot: :rotating_light: Alert 4212345678 - token_saturation_high detected in us-west-2. p95 latency up 2.3x on short-sequence routes; token_queue_depth > 95th pct. Paging @oncall-jordan and infra team.

oncall-jordan: Ack. I'm on it. Can someone grab the tenant breakdown and recent deploys?

sasha: Looking now — initial read: spike in ~128-token requests from tenant-acme starting 12:10 UTC, sustained QPS x6 above baseline. KV cache churn high (kv_miss_rate ~0.42). Worker pod pool showing token-processor backpressure on gpu-node-3.

sasha: Quick checks run:
```
rbctl query metrics --region us-west-2 --metric token_queue_depth --since 15m
rbctl logs deploy/inference-gpu-3 --tail 200 | grep "kv_cache_miss"
```

dan: Also seeing elevated user-space CPU on pod inference-gpu-3 (90%-95%) and degraded throughput on the small-seq path. No recent model deploys in the last 2 hours.

maya: Suggest mitigations: 1) route non-SLA traffic to fallback smaller variant, 2) lower per-connection concurrency for short-seq routes, 3) enable prefix cache for tenant-acme if not already. I can apply routing change for 20% to start.

oncall-jordan: Do it. Start with a conservative 20% reroute and drop max-concurrency from 4 -> 2 on the short-seq route. Please post the exact commands you run.

maya: Running now:
```
# route 20% of non-sla short-seq to rw-infer-small-v1
redwood route update --region us-west-2 --route short-seq --split "prod:80%,rw-infer-small-v1:20%"
# lower per-conn concurrency
redwood config set --route short-seq --max-concurrency 2
# enable prefix cache for tenant
redwood cache enable --tenant tenant-acme --policy prefix
```

maya: :white_check_mark: Changes applied. Traffic shifted — observing reduction in token_queue_depth within 3m. p95 trending down from 2.3x -> 1.4x.

product-tim: Thanks. Need quick summary for status page and customer comms — what's the impact window and ETA for recovery?

status-bot: Draft status update suggested:
"We are currently experiencing elevated latency for short-sequence inference requests in our us-west-2 region due to token processing saturation caused by a burst of short requests from a small number of tenants. Impact: increased response times and occasional request queuing for affected routes. Mitigation: we have shifted a portion of traffic to a smaller model variant and reduced per-connection concurrency; additional cache rules were applied. Current status: service performance improving; p95 latency decreased by ~40% since mitigation. ETA: continued monitoring; targeted full recovery within 60 minutes."

product-tim: For customer-facing email template (short):
"We've detected a performance degradation affecting short-sequence requests in us-west-2. We've put mitigations in place (traffic routing and cache changes) and are seeing improvements. We continue to monitor; we'll provide another update by <time+30m>. If you see anything urgent, reply to this thread or contact support."

oncall-jordan: Good. Assigning follow-ups:
- sasha: validate kv_miss_rate decline and confirm tenant-level cache applied (15m)
- dan: verify no node-level regression or cascading saturations (15m)
- maya: keep routing at 20% for 30m, then if stable, ramp down to 0/gradual rollback.

sasha: kv_miss_rate down to 0.08 after cache policy applied. tenant-acme traffic now hitting prefix cache ~85% of requests.

dan: node metrics look stable; no new pod OOMs or CPU spikes. throughput back to ~92% baseline.

oncall-jordan: Ok — status page update approved. Will post customer comms at +30m if no regression. Monitoring for 60m, will escalate to SRE lead if metrics budge >10% from current.

product-tim: Thanks team. Good template for future—we should add a short runbook section for token saturation events.

status-bot: Posted status page update (incident 4212345678) and queued customer email to affected customers (tenant-acme subset).

oncall-jordan: Closing note: keep an eye on small-seq QPS signals and KV cache hit ratio; if we see >2x again, prepare full reroute to fallback pool and notify sales for impacted accounts. :thumbsup:
